segments.body: Plurai builds a digital twin of the software, information and tools an agent would use, then maps possible task flows to identify edge cases. The startup says it can use those results to train smaller open-weight models and, in tests with Nvidia and Nebius, outperform some mid-tier frontier models at lower cost. Those results are not independent evidence of performance in wider deployment.

content.headline: Manchester United’s Monaco meeting puts Carrick’s future in the balance
content.shortHeadline: Man Utd’s Monaco meeting puts Carrick’s future in the balance
content.standfirst: Senior United executives are expected to recommend a change after a poor start to the season, but Michael Carrick has not been told he is leaving. Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the Glazer family have a say in the decision.

image.caption: Sir Jim Ratcliffe, Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox, who are due to discuss Michael Carrick’s future.

sources.originalTitle: The Monaco summit that will decide the future of Carrick and Man Utd
Pochettino, Howe, Emery... or Carrick? Man Utd's managerial options

segments.body: Chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox are due to meet minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe in Monaco on Wednesday. Their recommendation is expected to be that Carrick goes, but no decision has been announced and Carrick is continuing to work.

segments.title: What could happen next
segments.body: United are 18th after winning one of their first 10 league games. Another option under consideration is adding coaching support rather than replacing Carrick; Bayern Munich coach Aaron Danks, who worked with him at Middlesbrough, is one possibility.

perspectives.body: BBC Sport’s review of possible replacements notes that Eddie Howe is available, while Mauricio Pochettino is contracted to the United States through 2030 and has a reported $10m release clause. Neither has been appointed.

content.headline: Clarke calls for sandpaper inquiry to be reopened after Khawaja’s claims
content.shortHeadline: Clarke calls for sandpaper inquiry to be reopened
content.standfirst: Former Australia captain Michael Clarke wants the 2018 investigation revisited after Usman Khawaja’s claims. Cricket Australia says it sees no compelling reason to reopen the case, while Mitchell Starc maintains the bowlers’ account.

image.caption: Michael Clarke, the former Australia captain calling for the investigation to be reopened.

sources.originalTitle: Australia fans 'can't trust what's real' - Clarke
Australia doomed to live with stench of sandpapergate
Khawaja alleges racial abuse by MCC member

segments.body: Clarke says Australian supporters cannot know the truth until the investigation into the 2018 ball-tampering scandal is reopened. Khawaja has said the whole team knew about the sandpaper, while David Warner has backed his account. Cricket Australia says its position has not changed; Starc says the bowlers were unaware sandpaper was taken on to the field.

perspectives.body: BBC Sport’s Stephan Shemilt argues that Khawaja has renewed the dispute without naming individuals, leaving competing accounts and unanswered questions about the original investigation.

segments.title: A separate allegation
segments.body: In his autobiography, Khawaja also alleges that an MCC member racially abused him during the 2023 Ashes Test at Lord’s. The MCC had already expelled one member and suspended two others over abusive, offensive or inappropriate conduct during the incident.

content.headline: Noskova beats Gauff to become first WTA Finals semi-finalist
content.shortHeadline: Noskova beats Gauff to reach WTA Finals semi-finals
content.standfirst: The Wimbledon champion produced a commanding performance to win 6-3 6-3 and reach the last four on her WTA Finals debut. Jessica Pegula also secured her first win since September, eliminating alternate Marta Kostyuk.

image.caption: Linda Noskova, who won Wimbledon before reaching the WTA Finals semi-finals.

sources.originalTitle: Brilliant Noskova dismantles Gauff to reach WTA Finals last four

segments.body: Linda Noskova beat Coco Gauff 6-3 6-3 to become the first player through to the WTA Finals semi-finals. The 21-year-old served strongly, broke Gauff four times in the first set and sealed the match with an ace.

Earlier, Jessica Pegula beat Kostyuk 6-2 7-5 for her first win since September. The Ukrainian alternate, dealing with a wrist injury, had already lost to Noskova and is eliminated; Gauff and Pegula can still qualify.

content.headline: Fans pay tribute to Tenerife striker Jesús de Miguel after his death
content.shortHeadline: Fans pay tribute to Tenerife striker Jesús de Miguel
content.standfirst: Supporters gathered to remember the Tenerife player, who died after suffering a serious injury during a Spanish second-division match.

sources.originalTitle: Fans pay respects to Tenerife's De Miguel

segments.body: Fans gathered to pay their respects to Tenerife striker Jesús de Miguel after he died following a serious injury during a match in Spain’s second division.

content.headline: McTominay reveals heart treatment before Scotland’s World Cup opener
content.shortHeadline: McTominay reveals heart treatment before World Cup opener
content.standfirst: The Napoli midfielder says he received treatment for an irregular heartbeat two days before Scotland’s win over Haiti. Now back in the squad, he has been named among the leaders his new coach will rely on.

sources.originalTitle: McTominay reveals heart treatment at World Cup
Pocognoli to lean on Scotland's 'captain group of five'

segments.body: Scott McTominay says he was put to sleep and treated for an irregular heartbeat two days before Scotland’s 1-0 World Cup win over Haiti in June. He has since had an ablation procedure in Manchester and says he is feeling much better.

segments.title: A role in Pocognoli’s plans
segments.body: Scotland coach Sebastien Pocognoli says McTominay is one of a “captain group of five” he trusts to help carry his instructions onto the pitch. Scotland need at least four points from their final two Nations League matches to have a chance of reaching a promotion play-off.

content.headline: James Hill earns first England call-up after Konsa ruled out
content.shortHeadline: Hill earns first England call-up after Konsa ruled out
content.standfirst: The Bournemouth defender has joined Thomas Tuchel’s squad for Thursday’s Nations League match against Croatia. Hill has played every minute of Bournemouth’s Premier League season.

sources.originalTitle: Hill gets first England call-up as Konsa cover

segments.body: James Hill has received his first senior England call-up after Ezri Konsa was ruled out of Thursday’s match against Croatia at Wembley. The 24-year-old Bournemouth centre-back has featured in every Premier League game this season and every match of the club’s Europa League campaign.

content.headline: Manchester City claim first Women’s Champions League win; Chelsea held
content.shortHeadline: Man City win in Europe as Chelsea are held by Häcken
content.standfirst: City came from behind to beat Inter Milan for their first Champions League victory of the season. Chelsea were frustrated in a goalless draw with Häcken.

sources.originalTitle: Women's Football

segments.body: Manchester City recovered from going behind to beat Inter Milan and secure their first Women’s Champions League win of the season. Chelsea, meanwhile, were held to a 0-0 draw by Häcken.

content.headline: McIlroy targets eighth Race to Dubai title as DeChambeau weighs options
content.shortHeadline: McIlroy targets eighth Race to Dubai title
content.standfirst: McIlroy says victory in Dubai would secure a fifth straight season-long crown, but he starts 533 points behind leader Eugenio Chacarra. He also says Bryson DeChambeau has few options for playing competitive golf.

image.caption: Rory McIlroy speaking in Dubai before the DP World Tour Championship.

sources.originalTitle: DeChambeau running out of options - McIlroy

segments.body: Nine players can still win the Race to Dubai at the season-ending DP World Tour Championship. McIlroy trails Chacarra by 533 points and would guarantee a fifth consecutive title with a win. An eighth season-long crown would draw him level with Colin Montgomerie’s career total.

segments.title: DeChambeau’s next step
segments.body: McIlroy says DeChambeau’s name could attract more attention to the DP World Tour, but believes the American has few options if he wants to play competitively. DeChambeau’s future is uncertain following the collapse of LIV Golf; he can apply for DP World Tour membership as a recent major champion.
